description: The graph illustrates the training loss over the course of model training for six different configurations, each representing a combination of model architecture (ChemBART, ChemBERTa, ChemLLaMA) and size (Small, Medium), all trained on a dataset of 20 million samples. The x-axis, labeled "Step," represents the number of training steps, ranging from 0 to 440,000, with major tick marks at intervals of 40,000. The y-axis, labeled "Train Loss," measures the loss value, which ranges from 0.0 to 0.85. The plot shows that all models begin with a high training loss, starting near 0.75, and experience a rapid initial decrease in loss within the first 20,000 steps. After this initial drop, the loss for all models stabilizes and fluctuates at a much lower level, generally between 0.2 and 0.4, for the remainder of the training. The lines for the different models are closely clustered, indicating similar training dynamics, with the ChemBART Small 20M (red) and ChemBERTa Small 20M (green) models showing slightly higher loss values than the others in the later stages of training. The legend in the upper right corner identifies each line by its color and corresponding model configuration.
